transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Daniel Cho, Priya Nair (Redwood); Tom Reed, Maya Singh, Carlos Ortiz (Sable)

Summary: Quick discovery to map Sable's integration surface — aiming to decide between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Focus on SDKs, Lang Chain / Llama Index adapters, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits and observability hooks.

Topics: SDK compatibility, LangChain/LlamaIndex connector work, gateway sidecar vs central proxy, quotas/rate limits, observability/tracing, security (KMS, SSO), POC scope and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time, uh this is Ava with Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
[00:08] Tom: yeah tom reed, CTO at Sable, maya and carlos with me, we run the platform team and the ml infra.
[00:15] Maya: hi all
[00:16] Carlos: hey
[00:20] Daniel: Daniel Cho, solutions eng, i'll mostly cover the integration bits and the demo stuff later.
[00:28] Ava: cool, goal for today is to understand your stack and what success looks like so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private. and, uh, call out any blockers for a pilot.
[00:38] Tom: great, we already are evaluating a few vendors, want to get practical — our main questions are around how the SDKs fit into our gateway and how to use Lang Chain and Llama Index w/ your runtime. latency and cost are big.
[00:50] Daniel: sure. quick q - what are your current request volumes and p95?
[00:54] Maya: right now, peak is about 450 rps for text-gen-ish workloads, p95 for our local microservice is 280ms but includes pre/post processing. for model inference we see around 800-900ms p95 on our current hosted provider for a 8k context model.
[01:14] Ava: ok that's helpful. are you open to using Redwood Hosted for initial rollout or do you require dedicated capacity because of data residency or regulatory constraints?
[01:23] Tom: we prefer isolated capacity but not required yet, it's more about auditability and KMS integration. we also have a compliance window — SOC2 and internal audits.
[01:33] Priya: to add, we support customer-managed keys in Private mode — that's often the reason teams move to Private.
[01:40] Maya: can you explain the difference in integration work for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? like code changes and infra?
[01:47] Daniel: yeah so, short version: Hosted is API-first, minimal infra changes — you hit Redwood endpoints with our SDK or REST. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools under your tenancy and some routing controls, you still use same SDKs. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds networking setup — peered VPC or on-prem connector — and usually more ops work but full control over KMS and audit logs.
[02:09] Tom: what about using Lang Chain / LlamaIndex? we have a lot of retrieval augmented generation with vector stores.
[02:15] Daniel: we have official SDKs and example adapters — small caveat, some community libraries call models via direct HTTP so you'll want the Redwood client layer in between for token accounting and observability hooks. we provide LangChain chains and LlamaIndex connectors in our samples repo.
[02:30] Maya: is that repo public? can we see code examples for batching/streaming and chunking for long context?
[02:36] Daniel: yes i'll share a sample repo link. it includes an example Lang Chain agent and a Llama Index loader configured for KV cache and prefix caching. note: transcriptions sometimes show KV as K V in docs but it's the same.
[02:50] Carlos: on the gateway side, we prefer a sidecar pattern to central proxy, do you have guidance?
[02:55] Daniel: both patterns are supported. sidecar gives you per-service controls and local caching, central gateway is easier for enforcing global quotas and shared batching. we also have a lightweight proxy example that preserves headers for trace ids and integrates with Redwood's observability hooks.
[03:12] Tom: how granular are your rate limits and quotas? can we do per-customer, per-route, and per-model quotas?
[03:18] Ava: yes all of those. you can set token-based and request-based quotas, route-level limits, and token caps per model. we also support burst windows for short spikes.
[03:28] Maya: do you expose rate-limit headers so our gateway can surface them to internal callers?
[03:32] Daniel: yep x-rw-remaining, x-rw-limit, etc — standard. and we provide webhook hooks for quota-exhaust events so you can trigger fallbacks.
[03:42] Carlos: observability — what traces/metrics do you emit, and can we integrate with our Datadog and internal tracing?
[03:48] Daniel: we emit per-request latency, model selection, batch sizes, token counts and cost breakdown. we have an OTLP-compatible exporter and logs can go to your SIEM. our console has per-token cost and per-route p95 dashboards.
[04:05] Tom: security: SSO for console, RBAC for users, and support for customer KMS?
[04:10] Priya: yes SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and KMS integrations. in Private mode you can use your HSM via the connector. we'll send the security pack after.
[04:20] Maya: any gotchas with LangChain regarding function calling or streaming?
[04:24] Daniel: function calling works with our streaming APIs. Lang Chain's callback handlers sometimes need small adapters — mostly glue code to handle chunked streaming and function call events. that's in the sample repo.
[04:38] [crosstalk, faint] Tom: uh, what's the typical time to spin up dedicated capacity?
[04:43] Ava: with committed slots we can provision in a few hours to a day depending on region and GPU type. initial onboarding may take a week including routing and tests.
[04:52] Carlos: and private?
[04:53] Priya: Private VPC peering usually takes 2-3 weeks to validate networking plus your security review and KMS key exchange. on-prem longer.
[05:03] Maya: cost question — how does batching affect per-token pricing? we want to understand cost savings without sacrificing latency.
[05:10] Daniel: batching and KV/prefix caching reduce token compute — depending on your distribution you can see 20-60% cost reduction. our Optimize tool will recommend batch sizes and quantization profiles by workload. note that large batching trades off some tail latency.
[05:27] Tom: do you have any customers using LlamaIndex at scale with Redwood?
[05:31] Daniel: yes a few; they run the retrievals locally and call Redwood for generation with cached KV tokens to reduce regen. we'll anonymize case studies.
[05:40] Maya: on the integration effort — what does a 2-week POC look like?
[05:44] Ava: typical POC: week 1 - connect staging traffic, run sample prompt set and integrate SDKs and LangChain adapters; week 2 - run load / latency tests, evaluate QoE and cost, tune batching and quotas. deliverables include a short findings doc and a go/no-go recommendation.
[06:00] Tom: ok ideal timeline is to decide by end of month — we have budget cycle next quarter.
[06:05] Ava: noted.
[06:07] [long section of questions about edge cases and technical nitpicks omitted for brevity]
[18:12] Maya: small thing — we use an internal vector store that exposes an embedding endpoint. can we host embeddings on Redwood or do we call external vector db and pass vectors into the model?
[18:22] Daniel: Redwood supports embeddings as a service, you can either store embeddings externally or use our embeddings pipeline. many teams keep vectors in their vector store and send top-k context to the model; both are supported. be mindful of tokenization and embedding dimension compat.
[18:40] Carlos: what about long-running conversations and KV cache eviction policies?
[18:45] Daniel: you can manage session KV caches in the SDK; we have TTLs and LRU-like policies. if you pin sessions in Dedicated you can store large context more cheaply.
[18:58] Tom: we're also curious about fallbacks — suppose a dedicated node is overloaded, how does Redwood route to a cheaper model or to hosted?
[19:06] Priya: smart routing policy can fallback to model variants or other regions; you can set tiered fallbacks: first attempt same model in another pool, then lower-capacity variant, then a faster but lower-quality hosted variant.
[19:22] Maya: are there any limitations with function calling when falling back?
[19:26] Daniel: function calling still works but you should handle partial outputs; our SDK surfaces reason codes for fallbacks so your app can detect degraded output.
[19:35] Tom: procurement question — do you support custom contract terms and an annual commitment for Dedicated?
[19:40] Ava: yes we do enterprise contracts for Dedicated and Private, with SLAs for uptime and latency tiers.
[19:46] Carlos: will we get tenant-level billing detail?
[19:48] Ava: yes per-token billing by route and model, plus cost-breakdown export.
[19:55] Maya: helpful.
[19:58] [pause, background noise]
[20:10] Daniel: i want to call out a small integration pitfall: some customers put Redwood behind an internal gateway and accidentally strip tracing headers; that breaks our observability. ensure passthrough of trace and x-rw headers.
[20:28] Tom: noted. we'll audit our gateway.
[20:32] Maya: about telemetry retention — can we get raw request logs for 90 days?
[20:36] Priya: retention is configurable; for Private customers you can push logs to your SIEM for long-term retention. hosted defaults to 30 days but enterprise addons available.
[20:49] Tom: LD (load) testing — will you support synthetic load from AWS region near us?
[20:54] Ava: we can coordinate a load window for POC. Daniel will share a load plan and sample scripts.
[21:02] Daniel: yes i'll attach a k6 script and a small LangChain sample that uses streaming.
[21:08] Maya: ok i'm concerned about bursts that cause quota throttles — how quickly can we raise limits during a test?
[21:14] Ava: for POC we usually allow elevated burst windows, production depends on committed capacity.
[21:20] Tom: anything else on compliance? do you provide audit logs for model inputs/outputs?
[21:26] Priya: we provide audit logs; you can opt into redaction of PII. also key rotation is supported.
[21:35] Maya: excellent.
[21:37] [longer technical dive omitted in transcript export]
[48:05] Tom: to recap: we need pricing for hosted vs dedicated with burst and private estimates, the security packet, sample LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, and a load plan.
[48:18] Ava: yes we'll send those items. i'd like to propose a POC kickoff the week of 9/21, with an infra deep-dive scheduled with your platform team.
[48:28] Tom: sounds good.
[48:30] Maya: ok thanks everyone.
[48:33] Ava: thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and links.

End notes: referenced artifacts to be shared in follow-up: pricing sheet, security packet (SOC2/ISO/KMS), LangChain + LlamaIndex sample repo, k6 load scripts, observability integration checklist.
